mentions.name: prereview
mentions.description: This tool speeds up the review-fix loop for LLM-generated artifacts from coding agents. Run it in a repo (or point it at a file, directory, or running dev server) and click what's wrong — a diff line, a markdown/html block, a region of an image, or a box on a live site — to leave a comment. Comments are written to a CSV that an LLM agent reads to make fixes and report back via comments or accept/reject suggestions. It ships with a Claude Code skill and uses an open CSV protocol so any LLM CLI can drive it. Ships as a single static Go binary, works fully offline, reviews docs/images/live UI as well as code, and comments re-anchor when files change. MIT licensed.
mentions.problem: Reviewing and refining AI coding agent output is slow and cumbersome — previously done by copy-pasting snippets, screenshotting the UI, and describing problems in prose one message at a time.
mentions.source_excerpt: so i built prereview to speed up that review-fix loop. you run it in your repo (or point it at a file, a dir, or a running dev server), click what's wrong: a diff line, a markdown/html block, a region of an image, a box on a live site — and leave a comment. the comments go to a csv, your agent reads it and fixes things and tells you what it did via a comment or even posts suggestions which you can accept or reject.
